title: Streaming session manager: cooperative cancellation, resumable retries, and ergonomic Go examples
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Customers using the Go SDK for long-lived streaming inference are encountering brittle behavior across three areas: 1) context/cancellation semantics (races when goroutines read/write after the caller cancels), 2) unclear retry rules for interrupted streams (how to resume vs restart without duplication), and 3) examples that conflate low-level stream management with application logic, leading to anti-patterns.

Goal: Implement a streaming session manager in the Go SDK that provides: cooperative cancellation primitives, a clear resumable-retry model with resume tokens and idempotency guidance, ergonomic helper types and examples for common patterns (simple echo, long-polling, reconnection with backoff), and tests proving deadline propagation and safety under cancellation. The feature should be backward-compatible: users can still use low-level stream APIs, but the session manager is the recommended higher-level API.

Non-goals: Implementing server-side resume protocols (server already supports resume tokens), changing wire protocol, or adding language-level changes outside the Go SDK in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: New package github.com/redwoodinference/go-sdk/streamsession with documented API and examples
Cancellation semantics demonstrably avoid post-cancel goroutine panics in unit tests and integration tests
Resume tokens are consumed/produced by the session manager; examples show resumable request flow without duplicate processing
Retry/backoff behavior configurable (exponential with jitter) and default settings are sensible for typical low-latency inference workloads
Cross-cutting tests cover deadline normalization, nested contexts, and partial response aggregation under cancellation
Documentation and a short migration guide added to SDK docs and one example in examples/streaming/resumable-echo.go
tasks: Design API sketch and circulate for review (PRD + sample code)
Implement session manager core: state machine for CONNECT, ACTIVE, PAUSED, CLOSED
Add cooperative cancellation helpers: SafeRecv(ctx), SafeSend(ctx)
Implement resume-token handling and idempotency guidelines in code and examples
Add configurable retry/backoff middleware and metrics hooks
Write unit tests (race, deadline edge cases) and integration test against local mock server
Docs: API reference, migration guide, and three examples (simple, reconnect, streaming-with-retries)
Code review, security review (if needed), and release notes
implementation_notes: API surface: type SessionManager struct { New(ctx, opts) *Session } and Session wraps StreamConn with methods Recv(ctx) (Message, error) and Send(ctx, Message) error
Cancellation: normalize incoming ctx by deriving child context with small cancel propagation window to avoid races when caller cancels immediately after Recv/Send returns

Retry semantics: classify idempotent vs non-idempotent streams. Provide ResumeToken type; server will accept resume tokens for partial-state streams. For non-idempotent operations, default behavior is fail-fast unless user opts into at-least-once resume
Backoff: default exponential base=100ms, max=8s, jitter=full; allow users to supply BackoffPolicy interface
Metrics: emit stream_connect_attempts, stream_resumes, stream_retries, stream_cancellation_reasons with tags (model, route, user_tier)
Edge cases: honor parent deadline if shorter than internal retry windows; ensure that a canceled Session does not leak goroutines by using sentinel channels and drained loops

Examples: show pattern where application logic reads from session.Recv(ctx) in a single goroutine, and session manages reconnect/retry transparently; include example using context.WithTimeout to enforce request-wide deadline
review_feedback: PM: prefer conservative defaults for resume to avoid accidental duplicate side effects; require explicit OptInResume for non-idempotent routes
Design: add explicit CancelWithDrain(ctx) helper so callers can request graceful drain on shutdown
Security: confirm resume tokens are scoped and short-lived; avoid storing raw tokens in logs
qa_plan: Unit tests for session state transitions and race detector enabled. Integration test that simulates network partition and server resume-token acceptance. Fuzz tests for malformed tokens and abrupt context cancellations. Run SDK conformance suite against local mock server. Perf test to ensure default backoff doesn't increase tail latency for 99th percentile under typical load.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind flag go_sdk_streamsession_enabled. Ship in go-sdk-0.9-beta, enable for subset of internal teams, collect metrics for stream_retries and cancellations for 2 weeks, then enable by default in go-sdk-0.9. Document migration steps and ship change log.
